source: Cambodia Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF), "ប្រព័ន្ធវប្បកម្មដំណាំស្រូវ តាមគោលការណ៍ធម្មជាតិ (ប.វ.ស)" [System of Rice Intensification Following Natural Principles / SRI], 14-page Khmer-language handout/booklet, undated, no author or elibrary URL visible on any page (footer reads "កំរណ៉ការអភិវ័ទ្ធន៍វិស្ស័យកសិកម្ម ខែត្តកំពងចាម" = "Agricultural Extension/Skills Development Office, Kampong Cham province")
text:
Main field land preparation (per the source document): plow the field thoroughly, multiple passes, to a depth of about 15 cm, then harrow to break up clods and produce a smooth, level soil surface. Drain excess water and work crop residue/organic matter well into the soil before transplanting. Apply natural/organic fertilizer, especially well-decomposed compost. Level the field well so that irrigation water can be distributed evenly.

Rationale for using organic/natural fertilizer, as stated in the source: it makes the soil more fertile; it helps the soil retain moisture longer; it helps build up soil fertility over time; it reduces the cost of buying chemical fertilizer; and it helps protect the environment.

Application rate given for organic/basal fertilizer: about 10-20 tons per hectare, applied and worked into the soil roughly 10-15 days before use/planting.

Types of natural fertilizer recommended in the source: animal manure, compost, and green manure (legume-family plants, grasses, and similar material plowed into the soil); rice straw and stubble are also mentioned as an important source of organic fertilizer.
